entry.title: ProQSAR accepted in the Journal of Cheminformatics

link.title: ProQSAR accepted in the Journal of Cheminformatics

entry.content:
Announcement

🎉 We are thrilled to share our latest publication: ProQSAR: A modular and reproducible framework for small-data QSAR modeling with fit-and-use models in the Journal of Cheminformatics. Published on 22 April 2026, this work presents a modular QSAR workbench built to support reproducible, risk-aware, and deployment-ready molecular property modeling.

🔍 With ProQSAR, we integrate the full QSAR workflow into one flexible framework: from standardization, descriptor generation, and group-aware splitting to feature selection, model training, statistical comparison, conformal prediction, and applicability-domain assessment.

📈 Across representative benchmarks, ProQSAR delivered strong and competitive performance across both regression and classification tasks. These results highlight the value of a modular and reproducible QSAR framework that not only supports accurate molecular property prediction, but also improves trustworthiness through calibrated uncertainty estimates, applicability-domain assessment, and transparent workflow tracking.

💕 Huge thanks to all collaborators on this work: Phuoc-Chung Van-Nguyen, Lai Hoang Son Le, Van-Thinh To, and everyone else who contributed to this project. I would also like to especially thank Phan Tieu Long and Truong Ngoc Tuyen for their supervision, guidance, and support throughout this work.

📄 Read the paper here: ProQSAR: A modular and reproducible framework for small-data QSAR modeling with fit-and-use models

💸This work has received support from the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) under the project entitled “Education and Research Capacity Building Project at University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City”, conducted from 2024 to 2025 (Project No. 2021-00020-3) (MEF 1).

For potential collaborations, please reach out to me or explore our work at MedAI.

CSC2026

By the way, I would also like to take this opportunity to promote another exciting event. TACsy PhD students are organizing the Computational Systems Chemistry Symposium on 29–30 June 2026. Feel free to register here: CSC2026, and please reach out to me if you would like to connect during the symposium to discuss further.
